# pipeline-rca Evaluation

## Skill Analysis

The `pipeline-rca` skill performs root cause analysis on a single CI/CD pipeline failure error group. It reads trace logs and preprocessed errors from an orchestrator-prepared workspace, investigates the underlying cause using log analysis and repository inspection, then produces structured section files and a `finding.json` with the diagnosis.

## Inputs

Each test case represents one error group with a workspace containing:

- `input.yaml` — contains `prompt` field (always `/pipeline-rca`)
- `_context/rca-context.json` — group metadata (id, name, collections, actions, error_description), pipeline info (project_path, ref, sha), affected_jobs_table, file_paths_table, dependency_versions, repo_submodule_path, group_dir
- `pipeline-context.json` — pipeline-level metadata (id, url, ref, sha, job_summary)
- `groups/<group_id>/jobs/<job_id>-<job_name>/` — per-job directories with `trace.log`, `errors.txt`, `job-metadata.json`
- `annotations.yaml` — expected outcomes: difficulty, confidence_expected, has_resolution, cascade, group_consistency
- `finding-reference.json` and `sections-reference/` — gold standard outputs for comparison

## Outputs

Written into `groups/<group_id>/`:

- `finding.json` — structured finding with 13 required fields including group_id, title, confidence, collections, references, resources_used
- `sections/error-overview.md` — concise error symptom (5-20 lines, `error` fenced blocks)
- `sections/root-cause.md` — diagnostic analysis explaining WHY
- `sections/resolution.md` — (conditional) specific fix instructions
- `sections/feedback.md` — (conditional) process observations

## Pipeline Flow

1. Read `_context/rca-context.json` and `pipeline-context.json`
2. Read preprocessed `errors.txt` for each affected job
3. For deeper investigation, use log cleaner or targeted grep/sed on trace logs
4. Investigate repository configuration via local git or GitLab API
5. Compare errors across jobs to confirm shared root cause
6. Verify diagnosis before writing outputs
7. Write section files (error-overview, root-cause, optional resolution/feedback)
8. Write `finding.json` with all required fields

## Quality Criteria

**Deterministic (check judges)**:
- `finding.json` passes schema validation (all required fields, valid enums)
- Required section files exist with meaningful content (>= 50 chars)
- `has_resolution_file` matches physical file existence and annotations
- Confidence level matches expected level (exact or adjacent)

**LLM judgment**:
- Root cause correctly identified (WHY not WHAT)
- Evidence quality (cited log lines and file paths)
- Confidence calibrated to evidence strength
- Section structure compliance (no headings, error blocks in overview)
- Resolution actionability when present
